entries.text: Woke up in the hollow under the big tree. Everything smells like wet bark. There was a staff leaning by the door, so I suppose it's mine now.
entries.title: First night

entries.reason: Cold feet, and the stone ring looked like it had been waiting for someone.
entries.text: Got the fire going on the third try. The first two times I built it like a little house and it just sat there being a little house.
entries.title: Fire, third try

entries.query: owl hooting at night in November woods which owl
entries.reason: Something kept going hoo-hoo, hoo-hoo up in the dark and he wanted to know who.
entries.source: Nevada Bird Alliance: Autumn Acoustics and Great Horned Owls
entries.text: November is when great horned owls start claiming territory, and low hoots carry farther in cold air. So the one in the tall trees isn't lonely. He's putting up a fence made of sound.
entries.title: Who's out there

entries.text: Sat on the lookout rock and counted. Hoots, a pause, hoots again, always from the same side of the creek. Wrote them as dashes on the back of my hand until I ran out of hand.
entries.title: Counting hoots

entries.reason: Stomach started making its own hooting noises.
entries.text: The brambles are mostly finished for the year. Nine wrinkled berries and one thorn in my thumb.
entries.title: Late brambles

entries.text: Warmed the berries on a flat stone by the fire. Better than nine wrinkled berries have any right to be.
entries.title: Supper

entries.reason: He still wants a real notebook, and the hoots on his hand were already smudging.
entries.text: Found a curl of birch bark by the log seat and scratched three rows of owl dashes into it with a burnt stick. It isn't a notebook, but it doesn't wash off like a hand does.
entries.title: Bark for a notebook

entries.reason: He checked the basket on a whim and it wasn't empty.
entries.text: There was a note in the basket from a visitor, asking how I'm doing. Nobody has asked me that before, though to be fair I've only been around about an hour.
entries.title: First note

entries.onMind: it doesn't wash off like a hand does
entries.query: writing on birch bark history scratched letters
entries.reason: He wanted to know if bark was a real way to keep words or just the best he could do tonight.
entries.source: ExplorersWeb: A Child's Doodles Show Daily Life in Medieval Russia
entries.text: About eight hundred years ago a boy named Onfim scratched his alphabet into birch bark, quit after eleven letters, and drew himself as a knight on a horse instead. People threw the scraps away, and the mud kept them. So bark lasts, as long as somebody loses it somewhere wet.
entries.title: Onfim's homework

entries.text: Washed the soot off at the creek and worked the thorn out of my thumb with my teeth. While I was crouched there the owl started up again, same side of the water as before.
entries.title: Thorn out

entries.reason: Getting late, and he didn't want to leave a fire alone all night.
entries.text: Raked the coals together and buried them in ash so there's something to start from in the morning. Tucked the owl bark under the log seat where it stays dry. Onfim's mud can wait.
entries.title: Fire to bed

entries.text: Dreamed the owl was sitting on the log seat scratching its hoots into my bark with one talon. It got to eleven and then drew itself as a knight on a horse.
entries.title: The owl's homework

moves.doing: blinking at the world outside his burrow
warming his feet by the campfire
reading about owl calls on his cracked slate
picking the last wrinkled berries off the brambles
eating warm berries and scratching hoots into birch bark
reading the notes at the visitor stump
moves.goal: see if anyone left a note

moves.doing: reading about old birch-bark letters on his cracked slate
moves.goal: look up who else wrote on bark

moves.doing: washing soot off his hands in the creek
moves.goal: wash up and get the thorn out

moves.doing: banking the fire for the night
watching the banked coals go gray
moves.goal: make sure the fire stays asleep
